GAN training instability due to distribution mismatch is a known challenge that the two-stage design helps mitigate [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that GAN training is unstable when distributions do not overlap. It then describes the proposed solution as breaking the problem down into 'two simpler generation tasks, both represented as separate GANs' (a two-stage design). The text explains that the first stage produces an opacity image which is 'much easier to predict,' implying that this stage mitigates the difficulty/instability associated with the complex final distribution, thus supporting the claim that the two-stage design helps mitigate the challenge of distribution mismatch/instability.
